prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map shows a foreground clothing rack and hanging garments in the lower half of all five frames as the brightest regions, about 0.4–0.9 m directly in front of the camera wearer and within arm's reach, while a wall column and two mannequins on the right sit roughly 1.5–2.5 m away and separated from each other by about 0.8 m. A person wearing glasses stands behind the clothing rack on the left in frames 2, 4, and 5 at roughly 1.2–1.5 m from the camera wearer and about 0.5 m behind the rack, occluded from the shoulders down by the bar and garments; the mannequin on the far right in maroon is partially cut off by the right frame edge in frame 1, leaves the view in frames 2–4 as the camera pans left and pitches slightly, and re-enters in frame 5. The person behind the rack faces toward the rack and slightly right in frame 2, disappears below or behind the rack in frame 3, and reappears in frames 4 and 5 facing downward toward the garments within their arm's reach without looking at the camera wearer. Compared to the RGB image alone, the depth map clearly separates the near hanging clothes and right-side architectural column from the flat store window backdrop, confirming that the red circular graphic and mountain pattern are on a distant surface (>3 m) rather than 3D foreground objects. However, the depth map is unreliable around the person in frame 2 (where their head is nearly merged into the dark background depth), across the reflective glass window where depth values flatten to black, and along fine hanger hooks that blend into the rack bar.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates regions in the mid-ground (roughly 1.2–2.5 m away) against an unsegmented black foreground and background, but heavily misclassifies store fixtures and graphics across the five frames. Specifically, it labels the mannequin in the white-and-beige sweater (standing about 2 m away on the right of the window, facing away and to the left of the camera wearer) and its window reflection (0.3 m to its left) as multiple overlapping 'person' instances, and labels the second mannequin in maroon on the far right (about 1.8 m away, facing forward/left and partly out of view on the right edge in frames 1 and 5) as a 'person'. It also misclassifies the large red circular graphic on the background glass window (roughly 2.5–3 m away, above the clothing rack) as an 'umbrella' in frames 2 through 5, while failing to segment the foreground clothing rack and garments located 0.4–0.9 m in front of the camera wearer within arm's reach. The real person standing about 1.2–1.5 m away behind the left side of the rack (who faces the rack and looks downward rather than at the camera wearer, with the rack within their arm's reach) is fragmented into partial 'person' masks in frames 2 and 5 and completely missed in frame 4 due to heavy occlusion by the rack bar. While the masks help highlight the spatial contour of the far-right mannequin in frames 1 and 5 and trace the horizontal shift of the background window relative to the camera's left-to-right head rotation, the map is highly unreliable because it confuses mannequins, reflections, and 2D wall art with real people and umbrellas while omitting the nearest foreground obstacles.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank in frames 1, 2, and 5, and detects only sparse, distorted yellow body-skeleton keypoints in the lower-middle region of frames 3 and 4, with no magenta hand skeletons detected in any frame. In the RGB strip, a real person is visible behind the left side of the clothing rack at about 1.2–1.5 m distance in frames 2, 4, and 5 (facing the rack and looking down at the clothes within their arm's reach, occluded below the neck by the rack at 0.4–0.9 m), while two mannequins stand at 1.8–2.2 m on the right. Instead of tracking the real person's head and shoulders on the left, the pose estimator places tangled torso/limb keypoints onto the hanging sweaters and hangers in the foreground of frames 3 and 4 (roughly 0.5–0.8 m in front of the camera wearer, within arm's reach) and a stray keypoint near the white mannequin on the right. Consequently, the pose map provides almost no usable spatial information beyond indicating approximate locations where garment shapes resemble human shoulders in the lower foreground as the camera shifts. It is highly unreliable throughout the sequence, failing to detect the actual person in frames 2, 4, and 5 due to severe occlusion by the clothing rack and hallucinating body joints on inanimate hanging clothes in frames 3 and 4.
